newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Official sees African role in helping Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Official sees African role in helping Bosnia.

text.p: A senior African official said on Monday the European Union and the United States should involve Africa in efforts to maintain peace in Bosnia, saying the embattled continent had more experience in ethnic problems.

"We may have our own problems...and we are certainly struggling with some of them, but that doesn't mean we should not play some role around the world," Kaire Mbuende, executive secretary of the 12-member Southern African Development Community (SADC), told Reuters.
"We can contribute. Our politicians have, from our own recent history, more experience in resolving ethnic-based conflicts," he said ahead of a two-day SADC-EU foreign ministers' meeting.
"We shall be sharing some views on Bosnia too," he said of the conference, set to review political and business cooperation between the two regional organisations.

"We had the problems of Zimbabwe and Namibia's independence struggles, and then the big problem of apartheid. I think we have valid experiences to contribute from these," Mbuende said, justifying why Africa and the SADC should stretch itself before resolving the long-running strife in Angola.

"You don't abrogate your international duties because you have your own problems. In the case of Bosnia, we are not asking for military involvement. We are looking at counselling and promoting peaceful ethnic co-existence," he added.
On African conflicts, Mbuende said some EU members such as France and Belgium should use their political influence to help find lasting solutions for Angola and Burundi.
"That's the sort of political cooperation and dialogue we are hoping to promote here (at the conference)," he said.
The SADC comprises Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Mauritius, Namibia, Lesotho, Swaziland, Tanzania, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
